auth.installation.hero_title: Initialize a new Trinacria CMS instance
auth.installation.hero_body: Configure the site settings and the first administrator account to unlock the backoffice.
auth.installation.form_summary: Complete the two steps to initialise the CMS instance.
auth.installation.db_guide_body: Before running the installation flow, configure MongoDB in the environment file.
auth.installation.db_guide_form_summary: The CMS can start installation only after MongoDB connection settings are available.
auth.installation.db_guide_step_1: 1. Create or update the environment file with MONGO_URI. Use the split variables only as a fallback.
auth.installation.db_guide_step_2: 2. Save the file at this path:
auth.installation.db_guide_step_3: 3. Restart playground and backoffice, then reopen this page.
auth.installation.db_guide_restart_hint: After configuring and saving the .env file, restart the application to apply the changes.
auth.installation.highlight.single_windo: The installation endpoint is designed to be executed once, before the platform serves normal operator sessions.
auth.installation.highlight.seed.title: First operator seed
auth.installation.highlight.seed.text: The account created here becomes the first trusted operator of the CMS and unlocks the admin shell.
auth.installation.highlight.handoff.text: After bootstrap, the flow logs you in automatically so the backoffice can proceed without a second manual step.
auth.installation.highlight.kernel.title: Kernel-guided admin
auth.installation.highlight.kernel.text: Once installed, the backoffice is mounted by the admin kernel and follows the same plugin-driven runtime model.
auth.installation.footer: After the first bootstrap completes successfully, this screen is replaced by the normal operator login flow.
auth.installation.info: This action initialises the operator surface for the current CMS instance.
auth.installation.error.already_complete: This CMS instance has already been initialised.
auth.installation.error.server: The server did not complete installation. Please try again shortly.
auth.installation.error.network: Network error during installation. Check your connection and try again.
auth.installation.error.generic: Unable to complete installation. Please try again.
auth.installation.error.communication_bo: The backoffice cannot connect to the server. Check that the application is running and try again.
auth.installation.error.communication_de: Make sure the server is running and reload the page.
auth.installation.error.required_fields: Complete all required fields before continuing.

settings.policy.ownership.title: Plugin ownership is preserved
settings.policy.ownership.body: Settings writes preserve plugin ownership. Secret values can be replaced from the backoffice, but existing secret plaintext is never revealed through an admin session.
settings.policy.json_first.title: JSON-first inspection
settings.policy.json_first.body: Operators can still inspect definitions and resolved values, which is usually what matters for debugging configuration drift.
settings.inspect.title: Inspect setting

settings.write_flow.title: Owner-signed write handoff
settings.write_flow.summary: The backoffice does not write settings directly. Prepare the next non-secret value here, then hand the payload to the owner plugin so it can sign and execute the request.
settings.write_flow.draft_hint: Edit the non-secret JSON value to hand off. The request is only prepared, never executed from the admin session.
settings.write_flow.invalid_json: The draft value must be valid JSON before the handoff can be prepared.
